data.title: Prachin Buri factory probed over e-waste, wastewater
data.description: A factory in Kabin Buri district of Prachin Buri has been found handling electronic waste transported from Chon Buri and discharging wastewater behind its premises, prompting authorities to prepare health checks for nearby residents.

data.title: Exam-rigging suspects freed as investigators miss deadline
data.description: Three key suspects in the civil service exam-rigging scandal were released from prison on Friday after the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) failed to complete the investigation that would have supported their prosecution.

data.title: 11 foreign suspects arrested in nominee crackdown
data.description: Authorities on Saturday launched the eighth phase of a crackdown on illegal foreign property ownership, raiding 17 locations at four luxury housing estates in Bangkok and arresting 11 suspects, including Chinese nationals, with assets worth more than 6 billion baht seized.

data.title: IMF-World Bank meetings open to online viewers
data.description: The government is inviting the public to follow the IMF-World Bank annual meetings online for free from Monday, encouraging viewers to submit questions during the “Civil Society Townhall”.

data.title: Khao San bar closed after 31 test positive for drugs
data.description: Thirty-one people, including four aged under 20, tested positive for drugs after authorities raided a bar on Khao San Road in Bangkok early on Saturday.

data.title: Floods test Anutin and Chadchart
data.description: The recent Bangkok floods have opened a new political fault line between the national government and City Hall, putting Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt under scrutiny at the same time.

data.title: Alleged recruitment fraud trio freed over NACC delay
data.description: Three offenders in the government recruitment fraud case were released from prison yesterday after the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) reportedly failed to complete the investigation that would have supported their prosecution.

data.title: Govt mulls how to keep Thais safe
data.description: Labour Minister Julapun Amornvivat has discussed measures to strengthen the safety of about 68,000 Thai workers in Israel amid ongoing security risks, focusing on emergency preparedness, worker protection, and preventing illegal employment.

data.title: Yim Leak family asks UN to hold Thailand to its treaty commitments
data.description: Jared Genser, international counsel to Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and his wife, has asked two UN Special Rapporteurs to issue an urgent appeal to the Thai government over alleged human rights violations involving the family, including their seven-year-old son.

data.title: Floods test Anutin, Chadchart
data.description: The recent Bangkok floods have opened a new political fault line between the national government and City Hall, putting Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt under scrutiny at the same time.

data.title: Thai PBS seeks  audit clarification
data.description: Thai Public Broadcasting Service (Thai PBS) has clarified that it has not received any official audit findings from the State Audit Office (SAO) regarding reports that 10 executives and employees were ordered to pay 85.22 million baht in damages to the state.

data.title: Police widen probe into suspect IDs
data.description: Police are investigating four key suspects in an alleged civil registration fraud network in Chiang Rai, including a Chinese man whose bank accounts and his wife's recorded combined transactions of about 581 million baht.

data.title: City tops UK readers' poll
data.description: Bangkok has been named the world's best city for 2026, topping Condé Nast Traveller's UK Readers' Choice Awards and winning over UK travellers.

data.title: Krabi eyes boost from Russian tourists
data.description: Nine charter flights linking Krabi to four Russian cities this month will boost tourism and strengthen its role as a gateway to the Andaman coast, Deputy Transport Minister Phattrapong Phattraprasit said.

data.title: Suphajee backs B450 tourism fee plan
data.description: Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun has backed a proposal to impose a 450-baht tourism fee on foreign visitors.

data.title: Ekniti welcomes IMF boost
data.description: Hosting the IMF-World Bank 2026 Meetings will help enhance Thailand's image and strengthen its reputation as a world-class destination, says Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas.

data.title: Anutin ready for censure
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has dismissed concerns over an opposition no-confidence motion targeting 18 cabinet ministers, saying the government is ready to answer allegations and explain its performance to the public.

data.title: Ex-PTTEP exec returned in 'Rolls' case
data.description: A former executive of PTT Exploration and Production Plc (PTTEP), accused in a transnational bribery case involving Rolls-Royce, has been brought back to Thailand from Indonesia to face prosecution.

data.title: B100 commemorative coin for World Bank-IMF event
data.description: The Treasury Department will issue a commemorative coin for the 2026 International Monetary Fund-World Bank meetings, reviving a tradition from the country's first hosting in 1991.

data.title: Thai court dismisses detention challenge by Chinese reporter
data.description: A Thai court on Friday dismissed a challenge by a Chinese journalist over his prolonged detention in Bangkok, a day after authorities began proceedings to extradite him to China, his lawyer said.

data.title: Bangkok train fare subsidies to cost up to B5.8 billion
data.description: The Ministry of Transport will seek cabinet approval next month for a budget of between 5 billion and 5.8 billion baht to subsidise electric train fares ranging from 17 to 45 baht per trip.

data.title: Thailand, Timor-Leste agree to expand cooperation, speed up direct flights
data.description: Thailand and Timor-Leste have agreed to broaden cooperation in five areas, including speeding up the introduction of direct flights between Bangkok and Dili.

data.title: Gambling website slips past Thailand’s AI screening system
data.description: The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES) is investigating why its artificial intelligence (AI)-based screening system failed to detect Shuffle.com, an online gambling website reportedly linked to the husband of Bhumjaithai Party MP Suchada Zhang Thansap.

data.title: Anutin orders faster drainage and relief as floods ease
data.description: The overall flood situation has improved, with waters in Chachoengsao and Prachin Buri provinces beginning to recede, as the government steps up drainage and recovery efforts in affected areas, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Friday.

data.title: Benjakitti Park stays open but with limits during IMF-World Bank meetings
data.description: Visitors can still use Benjakitti Park daily from 4.30am to 10pm while Bangkok hosts the IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings, but several sections will be off limits and access will be tighter.

data.title: Heavy downpour warning for 7 provinces on weekend
data.description: Three eastern provinces and four in the Central Region could be inundated by heavy rain on the weekend, while some areas in Bangkok will also possibly face downpours, weathermen said on Friday.

data.title: Working groups to draw up 'open government' plans
data.description: Four working groups will develop proposals on corruption, environmental problems, public participation and access to justice as Thailand works on its next national action plan for open government.

data.title: Debt trapping younger Thais
data.description: Young Thais are entering debt at increasingly early ages, gaining access to credit cards, instalment plans and digital financial services before many have developed the financial discipline to manage them.

data.title: City Hall to clean up Rom Klao estate 'in 4-5 days'
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) has teamed up with the Defence Ministry to clean up Rom Klao Housing Estate in Lat Krabang district within four to five days as authorities step up drainage efforts in 80 communities still affected by flooding.

data.title: Govt defends  transfer of district chief
data.description: Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee has defended the transfer of Ban Sang district chief Setthawut Wonglerwut, saying the decision was based on reports from provincial officials and local leaders rather than political pressure.

data.title: Govt begins paying out flood relief
data.description: Authorities on Thursday began transferring the first flood relief payments, as more than 1.42 million households have registered for assistance through the Tang Rat app, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) said.

data.title: Chinese suspect arrested at airport
data.description: Immigration police have arrested a 51-year-old Chinese man wanted in China for alleged illegal fundraising and fraud after intercepting him at Suvarnabhumi airport.
